thread:
Jia: Quick heads-up — noticed a sizable NDCG@10 drop after switching to quantized-small reranker (int8) on the longtail holdout. Baseline float NDCG@10=0.432, int8=0.390. MRR@10 dropped 0.215 -> 0.178. Any ideas?
Sam: ugh, that's sizable. Is this reproducible on prod-candidate set or just synthetic negatives?
Jia: Good q — it's only on the 'synthetic_neg_v2' candidate pool used by the eval harness. Prod holdout (deduped candidates) shows smaller delta: 0.432 -> 0.420. So suspect candidate provenance mismatch.
Maria: :eyes: users are seeing more relevance flips in searches with lots of near-duplicates — could be related.
Alex: can you paste the eval command and a tiny sample of candidates? I recall we tweaked dedupe last month.
Jia: eval invocation I ran:
```
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rerank-small-quant --candidates synthetic_neg_v2 --holdout longtail --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42
```
Sample candidate list for q1234 (top 4):
1) docA (source: scraped)
2) docA_fuzzy (source: synthetic-duplicate)
3) docB
4) docC_sim
Looks like synthetic duplicates are paraphrases that create tokenization differences which interact poorly with quantization.
Sam: a few hypotheses: tokenizer parity mismatch between offline prep and runtime, KV-cache rounding artifact in quant kernels, or dedupe/normalization differences. Have we run a candidate-normalization parity check?
Jia: ran a quick parity diff on 1k samples: offline tokens vs runtime tokens differ for ~9% of candidates in synthetic_neg_v2. Example diffs in the next reply.
Alex: try re-running eval with --dedupe enabled to force candidate-level normalization at eval time. Command:
```
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rerank-small-quant --candidates synthetic_neg_v2 --holdout longtail --dedupe --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10
```
If NDCG recovers, we know provenance is the issue.
eval-bot: CI run queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/34922 — rerank-small-quant longtail dedupe-sanity
Sam: also run float baseline but fed with the same offline tokenization output as quant (i.e., mimic the offline pipeline at runtime) so we can separate tokenization vs quant effects.
Jia: scheduling three runs now: (1) quant + dedupe, (2) float with offline tokens, (3) quant on prod-candidate pool (deduped). ETA ~45m.
Maria: thanks — product impact if the regression holds. Keep us posted.
Alex: if this is provenance mismatch, we should add an onboarding contract test that fails if tokenization mismatch >1% between offline prep and runtime.
Jia: Agreed — opened a short RFC: https://go.redwood/reports/ONB-452 (draft).
Sam: tagging infra for kernel/ABI parity checks as well — @infra-team.
eval-bot: CI finished — run 34922 results: ndcg@10=0.418, mrr@10=0.183 (quant + dedupe). Details: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/34922/results
Jia: preliminary take — dedupe recovers most of the gap (float 0.432 -> quant+dedeupe 0.418). Still a small residual, so next step is the float-with-offline-tokenization run to isolate tokenization. I'll post the logs when done. :thinking_face:
